title: Separatedness from an affine open cover with affine overlaps and surjective restriction maps
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:V\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $V=\bigcup_{a\in A}V_a$ a covering of $V$ by affine open subschemes. Suppose that for all $a,b\in A$ the open subscheme $V_a\cap V_b$ is affine and the ring map $\mathcal O_V(V_a)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal O_V(V_b)\to\mathcal O_V(V_a\cap V_b)$, $x\otimes y\mapsto x|_{V_a\cap V_b}\cdot y|_{V_a\cap V_b}$, is surjective. Then $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], i.e. its diagonal $V\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated), part (2), lines 4157-4175, specialized to an affine base $S$ (every pair of affine opens of $V$ maps into the common affine open $S$)

proof.text: For a,b, let C be the subring closure of the two restriction images in the global sections of the overlap scheme. For each tensor t, the image of φ(t), transported by (V_a ∩ V_b).topIso.inv, lies in C: tensor induction uses closure under zero and sums, and the pure tensor case is the product of two generators. Scheme.homOfLE_appTop_topIso_inv identifies the transported restrictions with the appTop maps defining IsSeparatingPair. Surjectivity of φ and the topIso inverse identity imply C is the full ring. Thus every pair is a separating pair.

The set-theoretic covering equality gives TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover V_a. Apply the already proved source theorem Scheme.isSeparated_of_isSeparatingPair [lem-weil-pbc-separated-separating-pair-cover] with the affine-cover and affine-overlap hypotheses and the separating pairs of the preceding step. This proves Scheme.IsSeparated V.
Mathlib supplies IsSeparated f for every morphism from a separated scheme. Apply this instance to f:V→S. The affine-base hypothesis is retained in the unchanged signature but is not used.
